newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss police disperse angry farmers.
newsitem.headline: Swiss police disperse angry farmers.

text.p: Police used teargas and water cannon on Wednesday to disperse thousands of angry Swiss farmers protesting against plans to cut agriculture subsidies to offset a programme against mad cow disease.
The police moved in after demonstrators threw apples, wine bottles and firecrackers at Swiss federal parliament buildings in Berne and drove tractors around the capital.
A police spokesman said the crowd, estimated at 10,000, tried to storm government buildings.
Farmers are adamantly opposed to paying for a planned restructuring of the domestic meat market.
In a bid to wipe out mad cow disease, the cabinet has proposed the slaughter of 230,000 of the nation's 1.7 million cattle in the next three years at a cost of 320 million Swiss franc ($256 million).
But the programme against the disease, Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could also help to raise beef prices.
The cost of the programme would partly offset by cuts in milk subsidies.
Farmers estimate the plans would cost dairy farmers two centimes (1.6 cents) per litre of milk.
Switzerland, with 225 cases of BSE so far reported, is second only to Britain in the number of infected cattle.

Scientists have found evidence that BSE can be transmitted to humans. Some countries have banned imports of beef from Switzerland and the Swiss themselves are eating less beef. ($1 = 1.2520 Swiss francs)
